relevance_note: Letter describing two unrelated patients with PSTPIP1-associated PAMI syndrome: "Both patients have the same heterozygous E250K variant in PSTPIP1".
method_note: Read the whole letter by hand; rows written with a short Python script in the scratch directory, every value from my reading. Table 1 has patients as columns (column headers 'Patient 1', 'Patient 2'); spans quote the row label through the patient's cell. Patient 2's cells carry reference ranges in parentheses; Patient 1's mostly do not. In scope: Patient 1, Patient 2, three relatives of Patient 2 (mother with arthritis, tested negative; the second parent, tested negative, labelled 'parent of Patient 2' because the paper says only 'parents'; sister with alopecia areata, testing status not individually stated, the WES included 'members of his immediate family'), and one previously published person from reference [4] (variant E250K given; included under the v4 passing-mention rule). Tested-negative parents get no variant rows. Patient 1 has 'no family history of note'. is_proband left null for the two patients (neither is called proband/index case and this is a two-patient report). Variant is printed only as protein shorthand 'E250K' (no p., no transcript, no cDNA); recorded in variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated; variant type not stated. Pathogenicity for Patient 2 and the ref [4] patient taken from the Discussion sentence naming E250K as pathogenic. Numeric table values were not turned into features unless the text states the abnormality (e.g. Patient 2 calprotectin 385 (26–78) left 'not reported' for hypercalprotectinemia; Patient 1 LDH and immunoglobulin values with ranges not used beyond the text). Contradictions/discrepancies: (1) Patient 2 DNT: text 'mild increase in DNT population (1.5%)' vs Table 1 'Not detected' - both rows emitted (not a checklist item). (2) Patient 2 cytokines: text says IL-1β and IL-6 'were not elevated in plasma' but Table 1 gives IL-1β 2.6 (0.00–1.26) and IL-6 40.4 (0.09–7.26), above the printed ranges; recorded the text's excluded rows only. (3) Patient 1 IL-8: text says it 'did not differ from controls', Table gives 36.7 (0.00–33.01). (4) Patient 2 apoptosis: text says apoptosis studies normal, Table 1 says 'Not measured'. (5) Patient 1 serum zinc 185 in Table 1 vs 192 μmol/L in text (possibly separate measurements). Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27): negative ANA/anti-neutrophil antibody/RF, normal serum Fas ligand, normal TCRvβ repertoire/proliferation/apoptosis/SAP-XIAP-FOXP3 expression; Patient 2's normal sequencing of myelofibrosis/neutropenia genes not recorded as a phenotype. Patient 2 'painful polyarthropathy' and 'acneiform rash' were not mapped to the checklist arthritis and acne items (broader/different terms); 'diarrhea' not mapped to colitis. Patient 1 had a splenectomy but splenomegaly is not stated, so splenomegaly is not reported.
